author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian directory surfaces, the paged page and the machine-readable list, accept an optional specialty in the address and list only the veterinarians holding it. The match is on the whole name and ignores letter case. A blank value is ignored; no match yields an empty list.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-003] given a Specialty named in the address, when either surface (/vets.html or /vets) is opened, then only the veterinarians holding that Specialty are listed.
[REQ-VET-003] given a Specialty named in a different letter case from the stored name, when either surface is opened, then it matches.
[REQ-VET-003] given only the beginning of a Specialty's name, when either surface is opened, then no veterinarian matches on it.
[REQ-VET-003] given matching veterinarians spanning more than one page, when the paged directory is opened, then the page count covers only the matches.
[REQ-VET-003] given a filtered paged directory, when the reader follows any page link, then the next page keeps the same Specialty.
[REQ-VET-003] given a Specialty no veterinarian holds, when either surface is opened, then it succeeds (HTTP 200) with an empty list of veterinarians.
[REQ-VET-003] given an empty Specialty or one of only spaces, when either surface is opened, then every veterinarian is listed as without it.
non_goals: Any form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing the Specialty (owner: may come as a follow-up request).
Filtering by more than one Specialty at once.
notes: Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records; skipped. PRD edits: REQ-VET-003 (this slice) and REQ-VET-004 (machine-readable directory reinstated as a supported surface per intake decision 2; its unfiltered behavior already exists and is covered by the existing JSON test) in the Veterinarian directory section; edge cases 2-5 added; the stale 'known defect' edge case replaced; Superseded REQ-VET-002 entry updated to point at REQ-VET-004 while staying withdrawn; NG-9 row narrowed with non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-09-18-non-goal-narrow-veterinarian-search.md. The ADR index in docs/adr/README.md is outside this agent's write scope and needs the new row added by its owner. Reversible decisions taken by me: the filter and the reinstated JSON surface are two REQs (003, 004) because the filter spans both surfaces; a matching vet is listed with all its specialties; unknown specialty names and 'none' behave as no match; the JSON list stays unpaged. Open questions recorded in PRD Open Questions, left out of scope: whether spaces around a non-blank specialty are trimmed, multi-specialty filtering, and a page control. Implementer: do not pin the surrounding-space behavior in tests. Edge cases 2-5 in the PRD each want a test or a data-driven case.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice fits the existing vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure). There is no service layer: VetController binds the request and delegates to VetRepository, following the owner-search precedent (OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName to OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith). One piece is new ground: a caller-named filter value must not enter the unbounded, never-evicted `vets` JCache cache. That rule is recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-18-caller-named-vet-filters-bypass-the-cache.md. Repository: add filtered reads for the paged and unpaged surfaces. Use Spring Data derived queries with whole-name, case-insensitive equality on the Specialty name (e.g. findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase with Pageable, and a Collection-returning twin). Do not use Containing, StartingWith, or Like, so a prefix never matches and a caller's % or _ is never a wildcard. Put no @Cacheable on either filtered method. Controller: both handlers take an optional request-scoped String specialty. hasText decides filtered versus unfiltered, so a null, empty, or all-space value takes today's unfiltered path unchanged. That decision is binding, not a business rule (architecture-principles § Web controller row). Pass a non-blank value as bound. Surrounding-space trimming is a PRD open question, so do not strip it and do not pin it in tests. The HTML handler puts the effective specialty into the model. vetList.html page links must carry it through Thymeleaf's parameter syntax, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes the value, and must omit the parameter when it is absent. Never place the caller's value in a __${...}__ preprocessing expression or a concatenated URL string, as the adjacent integer links do. Preprocessing a request-derived string is a template-injection vector (security-principles § Realization: Injection, Cross-site scripting). An unknown name, including 'none', yields an empty page or list with HTTP 200 naturally; add no special case. Vet.specialties is EAGER and loaded separately from the filter join, so a matching Veterinarian is listed with every Specialty they hold (PRD edge case 4). IDE oracle not connected; this fit rests on grep and reads of VetController, VetRepository, Vet, CacheConfiguration, OwnerController, and vetList.html, which is the weaker basis.
integration_points: Binding, GET /vets.html: add an optional request-scoped String specialty (@RequestParam(required = false)) beside the existing int page. It binds no persisted type, so no disallow list is needed (security-principles § Realization, Mass assignment).
Binding, GET /vets: the same optional request-scoped String specialty. The response stays the unpaged Vets wrapper (REQ-VET-004, PRD edge case 5).

Double for the framework transport: MockMvc in VetControllerTests (the sanctioned transport double, testing-principles). It covers routing, the blank-means-absent branch, the model attributes, page links carrying the encoded specialty, JSON shape, empty-result HTTP 200, and page count over matches. The existing @MockitoBean VetRepository is the tolerated repository double there, and it only stubs the new filtered methods returning a Page or Collection. It must not be used to assert match semantics.

Double for the repository boundary: the real Spring Data implementation over the embedded H2 seed data, in ClinicServiceTests or a sibling @DataJpaTest. It pins whole-name matching, case-insensitive matching, no prefix match, an unknown name and 'none' matching nothing, distinct rows, and a count of matches only. Seed facts: surgery and dentistry each have two veterinarians, and radiology has one.
Cache: CacheConfiguration and the `vets` cache stay unchanged; filtered reads never reach it (ADR 2026-09-18-caller-named-vet-filters-bypass-the-cache).

patterns.description: Paged derived-query delegation from controller to repository, the shape the paged filtered read follows. Deliberately not mirrored: its StartingWith prefix match and its strip() normalization.
Existing findPaginated helper and page-size local; the filtered branch reuses the same page size and model-building helper.

risks.risk: Filtered vet directory path (system-design § Scale and Load, row 'Veterinarian directory narrowed to one Specialty') issues a join per request.
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: derived query with database-side paging, uncached; size is unrecorded, treated as bounded.

risks.risk: Caching the filtered read would let any caller grow the unbounded `vets` cache with distinct names (system-design § Threat Model, row 'Unbounded cache growth from caller-chosen keys').
risks.mitigation: No @Cacheable on filtered repository methods (ADR 2026-09-18-caller-named-vet-filters-bypass-the-cache); a reviewer finding otherwise blocks.

risks.risk: The caller-supplied Specialty is echoed into page-link URLs; copying the template's __${...}__ preprocessing pattern would evaluate request-derived text (security-principles § Realization, Injection and Cross-site scripting rows).
risks.mitigation: Thymeleaf link parameter syntax only, which encodes the value; the parameter is omitted when absent.

risks.risk: A join across the many-to-many association without DISTINCT would duplicate a Veterinarian or inflate the page count, breaking the acceptance criterion that the page count covers only matches.
risks.mitigation: Distinct derived query; the repository-level test asserts total count equals the number of matching Veterinarians.

risks.risk: Case-insensitive equality must behave the same on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL (system-design § Persistence notes per-vendor case handling for owners; see Known Defects).
risks.mitigation: IgnoreCase derived queries compare upper() on both sides in JPQL, independent of column collation; do not rely on a vendor collation.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-supplied specialty reaches only Spring Data derived queries (VetRepository.java: `Collection<Vet> findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String specialtyName)` and the Pageable overload), which bind it as a parameter. No query text is built from it. ClinicServiceTests pins that LIKE metacharacters do not act as wildcards (`@ValueSource(strings = { "cardiology", "none", "%", "radiolog_" })` expects empty results).

XSS and URL injection in vetList.html: the echoed specialty goes only into Thymeleaf link-expression parameters (`@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`), which URL-encode the value and HTML-escape the attribute. VetControllerTests pins this with `SPECIALTY_NEEDING_URL_ENCODING = "oral & dental"` rendered as `oral%20%26%20dental` behind `&specialty=`. The change also removes the `__${...}__` preprocessing from the vet pagination links. `grep -F -e '__$' src/main/resources/templates/` no longer matches vetList.html; the remaining preprocessing sites (ownersList.html, ownerDetails.html, layout.html, the field fragments) are outside this change and carry no request text from this slice.

Resource exhaustion: filtered reads carry no @Cacheable, so a caller who sends many different specialty names cannot grow the unbounded `vets` cache. The DB-side paged read keeps the HTML route bounded. The unpaged JSON route returns only the vets holding one specialty. The threat-model row and the ADR record this choice.

Input handling: a blank specialty falls back to the unfiltered path (`StringUtils.hasText(specialty) ? specialty : null`). The parameter is a plain String @RequestParam with no @ModelAttribute or @RequestBody binding target, so mass assignment does not apply. No logging, file I/O, shell, or deserialization code is added.
Credentials: `grep -E -i` over the added diff lines for password, secret, token, and api key returned no matches. build.gradle is not in the change set, so dependencies are unchanged.

Supply chain: `./gradlew dependencies` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, and tools.jackson jackson-databind 3.1.5. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (`grep -F -e dependencyCheck build.gradle` gives no match), so this review ran no NVD match.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The same conditional expression `${specialty == null} ? @{/vets.html(page=X)} : @{/vets.html(page=X,specialty=${specialty})}` is repeated at all five page-link sites (first/prev/next/last plus the page-number loop), differing only in the page number. Thymeleaf's `@{...}` syntax does not omit a null-valued parameter on its own (renders `?specialty=` instead of dropping it), so the conditional itself is necessary, but five copies of the same branching logic is the duplication the checklist's Control Flow bullet names ("A conditional repeated across sibling sites ... is duplication: compute it once and reference it").
findings.fix: Compute the specialty query-parameter fragment once with `th:with` (e.g. bind a single reusable expression or a small local variable holding whether specialty is present) and reference it at all five sites, or factor the five links into a Thymeleaf fragment parameterized by page number.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The specialty-carrying ternary (`${specialty == null} ? @{/vets.html(page=…)} : @{/vets.html(page=…,specialty=${specialty})}`) is duplicated across five link locations (the numbered page list, first, previous, next, last). `theFilteredVetDirectoryPageLinksShouldKeepTheSpecialty` exercises only the numbered-page-list branch (with `firstOfTwoPages()`, currentPage=1, so `first`/`previous` never even render). A copy-paste slip in the `next`, `last`, `first`, or `previous` branch (e.g. dropping the specialty clause) would ship undetected — no test would fail. This is a missing-test finding, not a defect found: extend the page-link fixture to a currentPage in the middle of >=3 pages so first/previous/next/last all render, and assert each carries the specialty parameter (or add a case per remaining link).

approved_aspects: Repository-boundary match semantics (whole-name, case-insensitive, no-prefix, unknown-name/'none'/wildcard-character non-match, distinct count, multi-specialty listing) are pinned once in ClinicServiceTests against the real Spring Data implementation and embedded H2 seed data (src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicServiceTests.java:239-285), matching the design-block's repository-boundary assignment.

IgnoreCase derives an equality match, not LIKE, so the ClinicServiceTests cases `"%"` and `"radiolog_"` in theSpecialtyFilterShouldYieldAnEmptyListWhenNoVetHoldsIt show that wildcard characters get no special meaning.

Output escaping: the only place the specialty is rendered is vetList.html:30 `th:href="${specialty == null} ? @{/vets.html(page=${target})} : @{/vets.html(page=${target},specialty=${specialty})}"`. The value is a link-expression parameter, which Thymeleaf URL-encodes and then attribute-escapes. everyFilteredVetDirectoryPageLinkShouldKeepTheSpecialty checks this with `oral & dental` rendering as `oral%20%26%20dental` behind `&`. `grep -rnF -e 'th:utext' src/main/resources/templates/` returned no hits.

The change weakens no existing control and actually removes Thymeleaf preprocessing: the old vetList.html page links `@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}` are replaced with parameterized link expressions. `grep -rnF -e '__${' src/main/resources/templates/` finds no remaining hit in vets/vetList.html. The hits that remain (ownersList.html, ownerDetails.html, the fragments) predate this change and render integers or template-fixed names, not request text.

Cache-growth DoS is closed: the filtered reads carry no @Cacheable (VetRepository.java diff: `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` only), so caller-chosen names cannot grow the unbounded `vets` cache. This matches the system-design.md:194 threat-model row and the new ADR.

Binding and mass assignment: the only new input is a scalar `@RequestParam(required = false) String specialty` on the two existing GET routes. No new @ModelAttribute or @RequestBody target is added, and no endpoint is added. Blank input becomes null through StringUtils.hasText (VetController.namedSpecialty), which keeps the unfiltered path. The filtered JSON route returns a subset of the already-unpaged unfiltered collection, so it adds no new unbounded read.

No secrets are introduced: build.gradle and application*.properties are unchanged (`git diff --stat HEAD -- build.gradle pom.xml src/main/resources/application*.properties` is empty), and the diff adds no credential-like literals. Supply chain: this change touches no dependency. No NVD match ran in this review because dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (`grep -nF -e dependencyCheck build.gradle` returned no hits). Resolved versions from `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath`: Spring Boot plugin 4.1.1 (build.gradle:5), jackson-databind 3.1.5 (tools.jackson.core), thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final.

author: change-grader
summary: filter the vet directory by one named specialty

blast_radius.note: Code reach is the vet package only: two new uncached derived queries on VetRepository, an optional parameter on both VetController routes, and a vetList.html page-link refactor. No sensitive paths are touched. Most of the 47 hunks are PRD, system-design, and ADR prose. The unfiltered paths still call the same cached findAll methods.

semantic_surprise.note: Reading the hunks turned up nothing unexpected. The blank check uses StringUtils.hasText and falls back to the old calls. The IgnoreCase query is an equality match, so the % and radiolog_ wildcard tests correctly return empty. The specialty only reaches the page through URL-encoding @{} links. The one unusual construct is a pageLink fragment defined inside a th:remove="all" span, which rewrites the existing unfiltered links too. Rendering tests pin both the filtered and unfiltered href forms.

test_adequacy.note: build_passed is true. The repository tests run the real derived queries on H2 and check whole-name versus prefix matching, case folding, LIKE wildcards, the "none" word, distinct page totals, and that a match keeps all its specialties. The MockMvc tests check blank and whitespace fallback on both routes, the empty-match 200, and that all six rendered page links on a middle page keep an encoded specialty. These tests would fail against a broken implementation.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched reviewers approved in round 2 with no findings and no recommendations. The round-1 changes_requested were three autofix-level items: template duplication, a link-coverage test gap, and doc wording. Each was addressed in the working tree.

scope_deviation.note: The owner's intake decisions explicitly cover narrowing NG-9, minting REQ-VET-004 for the reinstated /vets surface, and dropping its known-defect row. design_revisions=1 and the single build-failure came from an autofix-audit process loop, not a design mismatch. Open questions such as surrounding spaces and multiple specialties are recorded, not implemented.

rationale: A contained, well-tested filter: unfiltered paths keep their cached calls, filtered reads use equality and are not cached, and every page link is checked to keep the encoded specialty. Reviewers approved cleanly and the scope shifts are owner-decided. A glance at VetController and the vetList.html fragment is enough.
